titular: Alphabet plunges 12.6% and drags the Nasdaq down
resum: The Nasdaq fell 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.3% on Thursday, weighed down by the worst session in Alphabet's history after its results; Microsoft closed almost flat.
per_que_importa: If you have an index fund or a pension plan with US stocks, it has probably lost value this week: big tech carries a lot of weight in those indices.
xifra_text: Alphabet's fall on Thursday, the worst session in its history

titular: Amazon and Intel tumble after the close
resum: Amazon was down 7.3% after hours as AI spending squeezed its free cash flow, and Intel fell 23% after forecasting fourth-quarter revenue of $15–16bn.
per_que_importa: It shows the big question of the moment: tech companies are spending fortunes on AI and the market doesn't know whether it will pay off. If the doubts grow, the whole stock market feels it.
xifra_text: Intel's drop after hours following its results

titular: The ECB leaves interest rates unchanged
resum: The deposit rate stays at 2.50%, the main refinancing rate at 2.65% and the marginal lending rate at 2.90%.
per_que_importa: If you have a variable-rate mortgage, the ECB isn't making it more expensive today, but the market already expects a hike in December and the Euribor has already moved ahead of it.

titular: The Fed holds rates and US GDP grows 3.4%
resum: The Federal Reserve kept rates on hold on Wednesday, with two votes in favour of raising them; third-quarter GDP grew at an annualised 3.4% and September PCE inflation came in at 3.6%.
per_que_importa: A fast-growing economy with high inflation makes a Fed rate hike more likely, and that tends to make loans more expensive and push stock markets down around the world.
xifra_text: annualised US GDP growth in the third quarter

titular: BBVA earns €9,066m through September but falls on the stock market
resum: Profit rose 13.6% (€3,015m in the quarter, +14.4%), but the shares opened 5.4% lower because impairments rose 25.8%.
per_que_importa: A bank can earn more and still fall on the stock market: investors look mainly at the future, and here the worry is loans that may not be repaid.

titular: Spanish energy companies' profits soar on oil prices
resum: Iberdrola, Repsol, Naturgy and Endesa made a combined €14,542m through September (+47%); Repsol more than quadrupled its profit to €5,006m.
per_que_importa: Expensive oil fills energy companies' coffers, but it's the same thing that pushes up petrol, electricity and gas bills at home.
xifra_text: combined profit of Iberdrola, Repsol, Naturgy and Endesa

titular: Mixed day in Asia as the Kospi slumps and the BoJ meets
resum: The Kospi is down 5.4% and the Nikkei 2.6% on AI fears, while the Hang Seng gains 1.2%; the Bank of Japan wraps up its meeting today and no change is expected (rates at 1.25%).
per_que_importa: When Asian markets fall overnight, they often set the tone for how Europe opens in the morning.

resum: Brent rose 1.1% to $116.15 and WTI 1.05% to $103.07, on tension in the Middle East and the risk to supply.
per_que_importa: More expensive crude ends up at the petrol pump and in the gas bill; for now, Spain's cut in fuel tax is cushioning part of it.

titular: DoorDash to buy Instacart, and Thrive lands ADT
resum: DoorDash will pay $65 per Instacart share, mostly in cash, and rose 5.6%; ADT jumped 33% after Thrive offered $10 per share (a 45.6% premium).
per_que_importa: When one company buys another, it usually pays more than its market value; that's why the target's shares shoot up all at once.

titular: Today: BoJ decision, labour costs and Chicago PMI
resum: The US publishes the third-quarter employment cost index (13:30 Madrid time) and the Chicago PMI, and the Fed's Mary Daly and Alberto Musalem are due to speak.
per_que_importa: Today's US wage data will help show whether inflation there will come down and, therefore, whether the Fed will raise rates.
